questions.prompt: A class diagram shows a Component interface, a Leaf, and a Composite holding a collection of Components with Add/Remove. Pattern?
questions.explain: **Composite** diagram signature: Component / Leaf / Composite-with-child-aggregation. Observer's signature is Subject with Attach/Detach/Notify against IObserver.Update; Adapter realizes the Target AND wraps the Adaptee.

questions.prompt: A diagram shows class X realizing interface `ITarget` and holding a reference to class `LegacyLib` whose method names differ. Pattern?
questions.explain: **Adapter** = realizes Target + association to Adaptee, translating inside. (Drill Q13(v).)

questions.prompt: An e-commerce checkout calls inventory, payment, shipping and email subsystems through one `PlaceOrder()` method that hides the choreography. Pattern?
questions.explain: One simplified entry point over many subsystem APIs, no interface mismatch = **Facade**.

options: The Subject holds a list of observers behind an interface and calls Update on each in Notify — it never knows concrete observer classes
Observers poll the subject every second
Update is called by the observers themselves
questions.explain: Subject knows only **IObserver** — that's the decoupling. Notify (fired on real state change) loops the list calling Update. Polling is exactly what Observer eliminates.

questions.prompt: In the flight-status design, why does `VendorXAdapter` implement `IDisplay` rather than modify `VendorXPanel`?
options: The vendor class can't be modified; the adapter realizes the expected interface and converts Render(info) into panel.PushText(formatted)
Adapters are faster than direct calls
questions.explain: Classic Adapter constraint: the Adaptee is closed (vendor/legacy). The adapter is the bridge: `Render(info) => _panel.PushText(info.FlightNo + " : " + info.StatusText)` — and the Subject just sees another IDisplay observer.

questions.prompt: Which row classifies the patterns correctly?
options: Creational: Singleton/Factory/Builder/Prototype · Structural: Adapter/Composite/Facade · Behavioral: Observer/Iterator
Creational: Adapter/Facade · Structural: Singleton · Behavioral: Builder
questions.explain: **Creational** = object creation (Singleton, Factory, Abstract Factory, Builder, Prototype). **Structural** = composition (Adapter, Composite, Facade). **Behavioral** = interaction/responsibility (Observer, Iterator).

questions.prompt: A drawing app groups shapes; a group can contain shapes AND other groups, and `Move(dx,dy)` must work on anything selected. Also, every move must instantly refresh all open views of the document. Which TWO patterns?
questions.explain: Part-whole uniform operation = **Composite**; one-to-many auto-refresh of views on model change = **Observer**. Exam loves two-pattern scenarios — name both AND justify each with the signal phrase.

questions.prompt: In Adapter terminology, the existing incompatible class being wrapped is called the ______. (one word)
questions.explain: **Adaptee** (e.g. VendorXPanel / BillingApi); the interface clients expect is the **Target** (IDisplay/IDataSource); the converter in between is the **Adapter**.
